summary.prose: Building this Story means adding one new role entry, three new global config keys, a dedicated fail-closed parser and floor check, and two resolver functions (a pure synchronous selector and a bounded async availability probe) that together let an operator pin an independent security-reviewer model and guarantee it is either used exactly as configured or explicitly refused -- never silently substituted.

tasks.title: Register the 'security.review' role in role-taxonomy.ts
tasks.summary: Add one new RoleDescriptor entry {id:'security.review', criticality:'critical', defaultTier:'core'} to the closed ROLES array in src/config/role-taxonomy.ts, so the role participates in coreFloor protection and is exposed by settings-catalog.ts like every other critical role. Pure data addition -- no accessor logic changes.
acceptanceChecks: roleDescriptor('security.review') returns the registered descriptor with criticality:'critical' and defaultTier:'core'
Every existing role-taxonomy.test.ts assertion (e.g. 'critical role must default to core') still passes for the new entry
settings-catalog.ts's generic 'every critical role appears' assertion covers the new entry without any settings-catalog.ts code change

tasks.title: Add models.security.{runner,model,effort} global-only config-catalog rows
tasks.summary: Add three new GLOBAL-ONLY scalar rows to config-catalog.ts, mirroring the existing models.tiers.<tier>.{runner,model,effort} row shape exactly (same {path, type, default, desc, enumValues?, group} shape as buildConfigCatalog's tierRows/effortRow pattern), under a new group label (e.g. 'Models -- security'). No byRepo variant -- per-repo config only ever picks a TIER for a role, never the model behind it.
acceptanceChecks: config-catalog.ts exposes models.security.runner (enum of FamilyId), models.security.model (string), models.security.effort (enum, optional) as global-only rows
No byRepo.* variant exists for these three keys
settings-catalog.ts surfaces the new rows the same way it surfaces models.tiers.* rows, with no changes to how models.tiers.* itself is rendered

tests.name: CONFIG_CATALOG includes models.security.runner/model/effort as global-only rows with no byRepo variant

tasks.title: Add AnalyzeConfig.tiering.security + the tri-state parseSecurityModelPin parser
tasks.summary: Add a required, always-present tiering.security: SecurityModelPinResult tri-state field to AnalyzeConfig (corrected per LLD-0765b3a578e43eec-s1 revision 3: an optional field cannot distinguish absent from malformed, which resolveSecurityModelCandidate's fixed (cfg, registry) signature needs), populated by a NEW, dedicated parseSecurityModelPin(models: Record<string, unknown>) function in analyze.ts -- NOT a reuse of parseTieringOverride's existing silently-drops-to-undefined convention. Returns a tri-state result distinguishing {kind:'absent'} from {kind:'valid', runner, model, effort?} from {kind:'malformed', detail}.
acceptanceChecks: parseSecurityModelPin({}) -> {kind:'absent'}
parseSecurityModelPin({security:{runner:'cli-claude', model:'x'}}) -> {kind:'valid', runner:'cli-claude', model:'x'}
parseSecurityModelPin({security:{model:'x'}}) (runner missing) -> {kind:'malformed', detail}
parseSecurityModelPin({security:{runner:'not-a-family', model:'x'}}) -> {kind:'malformed', detail}
parseTieringOverride itself is untouched -- no shared logic or behavioral change to the existing tiers.* parsing path

parseSecurityModelPin: runner set with no model -> { kind: 'malformed', detail }

tasks.title: Add securityPinMeetsFloor eligibility check
tasks.summary: Add securityPinMeetsFloor(registry: ModelRegistry, familyId: FamilyId, modelId: string, floorTier: TierName): boolean -- holds iff some family's own FamilyDefinition.tierDefaults[tier].model (by id or alias) equals the pinned model AND that tier's rank is >= the floor tier's rank. A pin matching no family's tierDefaults at any tier is unclassifiable and treated as below-floor (false). This is the ONLY link between an arbitrary pinned pair and coreFloor's TierName ranking, since CoreFloorGuard.applyCoreFloor compares only TierName values and has no notion of an individual model's capability.
acceptanceChecks: A pin matching its OWN family's tierDefaults at a tier at/above the floor -> true
A pin matching a DIFFERENT family's tierDefaults at a tier at/above the floor -> true
A pin matching a tierDefaults entry BELOW the floor rank -> false
A pin matching no family's tierDefaults at any tier (unclassifiable) -> false

tests.name: securityPinMeetsFloor: a pin matching its own family's tierDefaults at a tier at/above the floor -> true
securityPinMeetsFloor: a pin matching a DIFFERENT family's tierDefaults at a tier at/above the floor -> true
securityPinMeetsFloor: a pin matching a tierDefaults entry BELOW the floor rank -> false
securityPinMeetsFloor: a pin matching no family's tierDefaults at any tier (unclassifiable) -> false

tasks.title: Implement resolveSecurityModelCandidate (pure, synchronous selection)
tasks.summary: function resolveSecurityModelCandidate(cfg: AnalyzeConfig, registry: ModelRegistry): SecurityModelCandidate. Resolves tiering.security (via parseSecurityModelPin's result already on cfg) or, if absent, the 'security.review' role's tier-default model; rejects immediately (status:'unavailable', no substitution) if malformed, unlisted, or failing securityPinMeetsFloor. Zero I/O, zero subprocess work.
acceptanceChecks: A valid, floor-eligible pin -> status:'candidate' with that (runner, model)
A malformed pin -> status:'unavailable' immediately, never falling through to the tier-default model
A valid but below-floor/unclassifiable pin -> status:'unavailable', never substituted
An absent pin falls through to the 'security.review' role's tier-default model as a normal candidate
An absent pin whose tier-default model is itself unlisted/below-floor -> status:'unavailable'

resolveSecurityModelCandidate: an absent pin whose tier-default model is itself unlisted/below-floor -> status:'unavailable'

tasks.title: Implement resolveSecurityModel (bounded async availability probe)
tasks.summary: function resolveSecurityModel(cfg, registry, opts: {deadlineMs, signal?}): Promise<SecurityModelSelection>. Calls resolveSecurityModelCandidate first; if already 'unavailable', returns immediately with no probe. Otherwise awaits exactly one bounded probe (a minimal CliProvider call) against the candidate, racing it against opts.deadlineMs and opts.signal; maps rejection/non-zero/ENOENT, timeout, and cancellation to distinct blockerReasons. Never rejects; always settles within opts.deadlineMs.
acceptanceChecks: Candidate already 'unavailable' -> resolves immediately, no probe attempted
Probe resolves successfully within the deadline -> status:'configured'
Probe rejects (simulated ENOENT/auth failure) -> status:'unavailable' with a backend-failure blockerReason
Probe neither resolves nor rejects before opts.deadlineMs -> status:'unavailable' with a timeout blockerReason
opts.signal aborted while the probe is outstanding -> status:'unavailable' with a cancellation blockerReason

Live (INSRC_LIVE_TESTS=1): a valid, listed, floor-eligible pin whose backend is deliberately unreachable resolves 'unavailable' with a populated blockerReason within the deadline, never a hang or silent substitution
